note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.
Every removal signal names its observing instrument (kogaki#113):
removal_instrument is `act: <the act that already happens and owes the
removal row>`, `none: <why no act in this repository can observe it>`,
or `probe: <tree-local shell predicate>` (exit 0 = the signal's
condition now holds; exit 1 = not yet; anything else = the probe could
not establish). Probes are evaluated by check-registry-conformance.sh,
which renders candidates report-only — removal stays a judgment.
Every admission record carries RE-EXECUTABLE EFFICACY EVIDENCE
(kogaki#243). The named defect above is a claim about what this check
CATCHES, and registration used to take it on the author's word —
constrain-generation applied to check EXISTENCE, never to check
EFFICACY. `efficacy` names the counterfactual instead: the case that
CONSTRUCTS the named defect and asserts the check REFUSES it.
`case: <path>::<verbatim label>` — the payload is the path, `::`,
and the label, WITH NOTHING APPENDED; human prose goes in the
sibling `efficacy_note`, on the convention `runtime_ms_note` sets.
`none: <why no counterfactual exists in this tree>` — the honest
state, and it is a MEASUREMENT rather than a deferral marker.
check-registry-conformance.sh refuses a `case:` unless <path> exists
and contains <label> literally and EXACTLY ONCE. What that buys,
claimed precisely because overstating it would be the very defect
kogaki#243 names: editing or deleting the cited text breaks the entry
that cites it, and a label too generic to identify one case is
refused as non-unique. What it does NOT decide: that the cited text
is a COMPLETE case label rather than part of one, or that it occurs
in code rather than in a comment. Both are judgments about meaning,
and a language-aware parser for them would be a lint over judgment.
Shape and resolution are gated; whether the counterfactual is a GOOD
one is judgment and is never gated — the split `probe:` runs under.

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive). Parses the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10) — request_id, outcome, one query line per framing, indented under line one, all OPTIONAL so every v1 receipt in git history stays valid — and widens malformed to SIX field defects, all conformance rather than counting: an outcome outside the hub's ratified triple (a bare `miss` collapses the two causes the 2026-08-02 correction separated), a re-framed outcome recording fewer than every framing's query, an `uncovered-after-N` whose N disagrees with the number of query lines recorded (shape validation alone let a receipt claim seven framings while recording two), an N below the two-framing floor (a miss is not recordable as uncovered until re-asked along another axis; the floor is stated as its own clause because it is currently also implied by the query rule, and an implied invariant is one a refactor drops unnoticed), and a PARTIAL v2 receipt — continuations stay optional so a v1 receipt is valid, but once ANY continuation is present the receipt owes all three fields SPEC §4 requires (PR #43 review). The embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation, and asserts the PARSED FIELDS rather than only counts — a count-only assertion cannot observe whether the continuation fields were read at all, which measured 2 of 8 v2 cases discriminating before the assertion was widened and 6 of 8 after. States what it does NOT verify: the query-count rule is satisfied by two rephrasings of one question, and axis-variation is a judgment no count can observe — the check asserts the framings were RECORDED and routes whether they differed to the review lane, with a receipt found carrying two rephrasings as the observation that would earn a real detector. Empty values are handled by ONE rule applied in the parse: continuation PRESENCE is recorded as a fact about the text rather than inferred from value truthiness, and an empty value is absent for every field alike — before which empty query lines counted as recorded framings, so `uncovered-after-3-framings` with three blank queries satisfied N == len() (PR #43 re-review), and a `query:` line holding a SERIALIZED TOOL ARGUMENT rather than a question (kogaki#160 finding 4): the field is defined at the consultation map's Miss-postmortem field as the question verbatim, the grammar accepted any non-empty value, and `query: {"tag":"lessons/claude-code-ops"}` shipped on master passing every clause above — because the transport DERIVED the line, reading it off policy_lookup's own `question` argument and falling back to the raw --args JSON for every other tool, so a gloss_index consult had no field in which to record its question. gateway-query.mjs now requires `--question` per `--args` and refuses without it, making the emission unproducible on the tool path; this clause is the floor under condition 2's marked-exception path, and is the narrowest rule that discriminates — a value that is a JSON object/array end to end is a tool argument, while a question CONTAINING braces or quotes passes, with fixtures in both directions. Backward compatible by the scan window: this check reads merge-base..HEAD plus the PR body, never a file on the default branch and never the whole history, so receipts already merged lie outside every future scan and no branch fails on work it did not author. THE SECOND AXIS (kogaki#268): a `disposition:` continuation key carrying the GATE half — what the gate did with the consultation — on its own field rather than in `outcome:`, which is where the digest's vocabulary claim assumed it lived and where this check's own ratified-triple clause refuses it. Three vocabularies in this seam are called `outcome` and two of them are mutually exclusive in one slot, so the resolution is one field per axis, each owned by whoever must agree on it: the values are ADOPTED verbatim from the ratified closed two-value set (`auto-resolved-FYI | escalated`, spec-policy-fork-consultation §"Amended 2026-07-21 (triage, #519)", "no consumer-local extension") because a field read by both sides of the boundary is the boundary's and the boundary's owner is the hub (`topics/knowledge-architecture.md:31@dec0d568`), while the field's SHAPE is this repository's. The key is OPTIONAL and is deliberately NOT added to presence-implies-completeness' owed set: most consults here are not fork gates, and requiring the field would force a value on them. Recognising the key in the checker is a REQUIREMENT rather than a convenience — the continuation scan stops at the first unrecognised indented key, so a receipt carrying `disposition:` above its query lines parsed on the pre-#268 scanner as a field-less v1 line with every later field silently dropped, and 10 of the 12 new fixtures fail that scanner spliced against this fixture table. What it does NOT make substantiable, stated rather than implied: `consult-miss` and `degraded` stay uncountable from receipts under this or any schema — an unconsulted fork emits no receipt and a degraded consult emits none by design — so both are refused as values with that reason named, and the report line counts the two dispositions and says what nothing here can count WIDENED (kogaki#336): the grammar gains a THIRD continuation key, `axis:`, and it is the first that binds PER QUERY — upward to the nearest preceding `query:`, first declaration wins, an axis before any query orphaned and reported. The check validates SHAPE ONLY — position and a non-empty token — because the `subject | conduct` value set is the hub's to ratify under the boundary-field rule (product-lab@4cc496b topics/knowledge-architecture.md:50), so any value passes and unknown ones are reported and denied nowhere; the report NAMES the distinct axes rather than only counting them, which is what makes an unratified set observable while it is unratified. Eight per-query binding cases exercise both directions, plus an explicit never-gates assertion that an unknown axis is not reported malformed — the assertion standing between shape-only and this repository silently minting boundary values it does not own. Runtime re-measured 80 -> 95 ms (three local runs) for the widening rather than for an admission, because the binding quantity is cost per ship-cycle rather than member count.

admission.contract: the client kit's install guarantees, fired rather than merely written: fresh-install layout, idempotency, the one-line degrade at exit 11, the pinless-body deny, harness-loadable skill frontmatter, the entry-2 boundary (no kit tool reads gateway state), and the absence of any colocation default. Also the transport's RECEIPT MODE (kogaki#66, story 1.20), where the emitter replaces hand transcription: the refusal to assign the `outcome` token — `deferred-slot: consult-outcome-token-assignment` is FILLED (owner decision 2026-08-06, kogaki#66 — the OPERATOR supplies the token), so a default would reinstate the guess the fill declined and the refusal must still name the slot rather than read as a syntax error; that a degraded run emits NO receipt block, because a receipt for a consult that did not happen is the fabrication the clause exists to prevent; that receipt mode is opt-in, so the pre-1.20 invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged; that the marked-exception key is the fixed UNINDENTED `consult-receipt:` token, which is correctness rather than style because check-consult-receipts.sh recognises only request_id/outcome/query as continuation keys and an unrecognised indented key above them ends the continuation scan, leaving a field-less v1 line that silently passes; and the emitter's own 13-case composition fixture pass, which asserts line one is COPIED from the served response rather than re-derived, one query line per framing actually run, pins merged under one commit, the token carried untouched, and five refusals where the wire did not carry what a receipt asserts. Also the consult ENTRY POINT (kogaki#94, story 1.21), whose properties are all properties of the INVOCATION rather than of the wire and so are decidable without a reachable gateway: that there is exactly ONE receipt composer and the entry point is not a second one, routing through the transport instead; that a verdict-shaped input is corrected AT THE POINT OF USE and never forwarded (exit 3), and that the correction is an affordance — `--restate` re-submits the corrected claim in the same act and the run then reaches the wire, which is the only observable distinguishing an affordance from a nicer denial; that `--outcome` is required at the entry point as on the transport, with the refusal naming the OPERATOR, because the entry point is the surface a session touches; that the two-framings floor is carried at the call in BOTH directions (refused with what the re-framing owes, and proceeding once the second framing is supplied), since a floor that refused everything would pass a one-directional test; that the framing COUNT is emitted as the transport fact it is and a token contradicting it is refused rather than repaired, repair being the tool assigning the token by the back door; that the re-framing bound is ONE, never a search loop; and that the exit-11 degraded path is STATED with its example receipt marker UNINDENTED above line one, asserted on the emitted text because a wrong example is a wrong receipt in every PR that follows it. What no case on either surface covers is a LIVE consult, which the test states rather than leaves to look covered. Registered because a test nothing invokes is the orphan-guard shape kogaki#6 was filed to end Also the ISSUE-CHECKPOINT CONTENT-LIVENESS half (kogaki#188), where the guarantee is that a pass-claim matches what was actually compared: that the THIRD entry point `--emit-pin-quotes` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade as the other two, because it is the WRITER for the stored quote hash and a writer that emits a short list on an unreachable seam reads as a complete one; and the tool's own content-liveness fixture pass, which is pure and gateway-free and asserts the whitespace-normalized hash (a reflowed served line is the same quote, while a case flip is not), use-vs-mention on BOTH the pin-quote and consulted grammars, a DECLARED served-address map that returns cannot-tell rather than guessing an address, the live topics/articles.md:79 drift blocked AND located at :80 as the regression pin (the dangerous form is the pin that still RESOLVES, so a resolution check cannot catch it), three results rather than two with `verified` reachable only through a fetch that returned records in scope, and an output that never implies liveness it did not check. Widened at this admission act rather than left to be inferred from the case list Also the SHAPE READ and the EMISSION DUTY (kogaki#325/#326, stories 1.48/1.49), the kit's two default-on consumer clauses, whose install-time properties are decidable without a reachable gateway and are therefore asserted here: that the shape read is gitignored EXACTLY ONCE across two installs and that the emission directory is NOT gitignored — the two assertions are deliberately INVERSE, because the artifacts answer the same axis oppositely on source sensitivity rather than on file kind, and asserting only one would leave a later change free to 'make them consistent' and destroy the distinction the spec exists to record, with the failure silent and, on a public repository, irreversible once pushed; that the managed CLAUDE.md block carries BOTH clauses, since specs/spec-client-kit/SPEC.md §2 refuses skill-as-sole-carrier and a clause reaching only the sittings that invoke a skill is the failure the default carrier exists to prevent; that the shape read degrades in ONE line at exit 11 like every other kit tool, which the install itself depends on because a hard failure there would break the ratified degraded-install-is-a-valid-install promise for every consumer; that the emission writer produces the five fixed fields at a dated, slugged path, prints that path as an in-session receipt, and refuses an undeclared grain, the set being closed like every other declaration here; that the emitted text ITSELF states it is a candidate and not a promotion, asserted on the artifact rather than trusted to the prose above it, because §4.2's emission-is-not-promotion boundary is this writer's entire standing; that the plain-register note REPORTS without refusing and the write still exits 0, a channel that rejects your words being a channel you stop using; and both tools' own gateway-free fixture passes. What no case here covers is a LIVE digest composition, which needs a reachable seam and is stated rather than left to look covered. Also the OWNER REGISTER's install-time half (kogaki#320, story 1.50): that the owner-render fixture pass runs; that the RELAY RULE in the installed skill points at the kit's emission and assigns the Conclusion to the agent — asserted against the INSTALLED copy, which is what caught this story editing the installed file while leaving the kit SOURCE untouched, the kogaki#285 divergence reproduced live and fixed in the same act; and that a DEGRADED consult emits NEITHER register, because a rendering of an answer that was never served is the same fabrication the no-receipt-on-degrade rule already forbids. Separability (AC2) is asserted where transportArgv lives rather than here — the entry point is not import-safe, so a node -e import cannot reach the function; this member invokes that pass and the arrangement is named in the test so the coverage stays findable. Also the DELTA STEP (kogaki#334, story 1.51), which is the shape read's §3.4 act and the first case here that needs a STUB GATEWAY: the earlier shape-read cases establish properties of a RENDERING, decidable from a degrade and a pure fixture pass, whereas a delta is a property of a COMPARISON against a live regeneration — a vendored pin differing from a served one — and no state of an unreachable gateway produces that, so the wire is doubled rather than the content asserted. Four properties, all on emitted text: that a stale vendored pin REPORTS AND EXITS 0, because §3.5's enhancer-never-dependency property makes a pre-step that gates a sitting the defect rather than the feature; that no vendored digest AT ALL is its own third state and also exits 0, an absent digest and an unchanged one being the same quiet and different facts; that the output is PIN-FREE — no `consulted:`, no `request_id:`, no `@<sha>` — because §8 puts pins on the machine-facing side and a delta shown before a sitting is the one shape-read output an owner reads directly, asserted on live text as well as in the fixture pass since the fixture composes its own inputs while this carries a real pin through the whole composer; and that `--delta` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade every other kit tool owes. Also the PER-TERM DENOMINATOR (§3.1's clause as amended by kogaki#334), which is the element-level three-state rendering PR #335 landed, surviving one grain down: `if (e.soft) continue;` made a term whose own `glossary_entry` read could not be parsed indistinguishable from one carrying no state line, so the section rendered its survivors as the whole in-scope set. The stub serves an unparseable body for one in-scope term and the case asserts that term is COUNTED AND NAMED in the digest — an end-to-end assertion the gateway-free fixtures cannot make, and the reason this widening is not simply more fixture cases.

admission.runtime_ms_note: RE-MEASURED at this admission act (kogaki#334), per the convention this entry itself states: a runtime is a measurement, and a stale number is stale rather than wrong. Three local runs, 8.24/8.46/8.38 s wall; the number below is that median. The +0.84 s over the previous 7536 covers cases 2i-2k TOGETHER, not only this story's: kogaki#320 added 2i/2j and did not re-measure, and 2k adds three `--delta` invocations of which two converse with a stubbed gateway over stdio rather than failing at spawn. The two widenings are not separated because the measurement cannot separate them after the fact, and inventing a split would be a number nobody measured. RE-MEASURING FOR A WIDENING RATHER THAN AN ADMISSION IS THE POINT: the binding quantity is total cost per ship-cycle rather than member count (`LESSONS.md:13@4cc496b`, `every-check-enters-with-a-budget-and-a-removal-signal`), so assertions added to an existing member spend budget with no count moving and are exactly the growth a count-shaped record cannot see — which is how a widening lands unmeasured, as 2i/2j just did. It is a LOCAL measurement and CI's runner is slower — the figure is a tier input, not a budget assertion, and this member stays pre-push. Re-measure at the next admission act that touches this check.

admission.contract: Terrain's three ported contracts over every survey record in the tree (manifest item 1, specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §2): completeness as a cover counted in placements — every Strand placed, no-relation Strands in an explicit named section, nothing silently dropped; the figure counted AFTER composition, recomputed here from the placements themselves, naming which family it counted; and navigation state carrying no narrowing key, so a survey record cannot smuggle the refused minimal-form bundling in as a field — plus the seam pin on every record. The detection half behind terrain/terrain.mjs's generation-time refusal (validateSurvey applies the same schema-carried rules before writing); the fixture pass is the evidence both halves discriminate. Carries composition FACTS only and says so in its own output; whether the grouping axis serves the owner and whether a ratified narrowing was worth taking are judgment and route to kogaki#13 PLUS the composition contracts the member has since grown to carry, named here because an admission record whose `contract` does not describe what the member covers is not recording what is carried (kogaki#145): §6.1/§6.2's co-tag screen — GroupClaim served first, member Lesson IDs for every group without --group, SubGroups judged at the screen with their leaf verdict and disclosures and a required judge pin, and no member-count threshold in the split logic; §7's claim lifecycle — the re-offer's three origin branches (record, screen-composed, absent) and whether an origin's member set was recorded or DERIVED; §9's screen-1 tag-row allowlist — the tag name and its Lesson count and nothing else, composed through the single `tagRow` constructor; and §12's Full Report — the identity triple (substrate pin, co-tag query, judge pin) with `none` typed, its four idempotence cases counted over real artifacts, and the eager --all-groups fan-out with its pre-write judge-pin refusal; and §8's `subdivide` COMMAND — the command path run end to end rather than only its exported composers, its record written past the instruments loop, the third instrument reading the judge's own verdict rather than a literal, and the PLACEMENT-COMPOSED `(fits no composed SubGroup)` SubGroup — EXPLICIT and named, which is the property the cover contract refuses to give up — carrying all three instruments (kogaki#165: from story 1.31 until that fix `subdivide` raised ReferenceError on every invocation, and no registered check invoked the command, so every exercised path masked a dead command); and §9's BOUNDED COMPOSITION INPUT — `compose-input`'s one tag-scoped shard pair per run with the journey half fetched only where a member carries one, its groups carrying IDS ONLY so a per-group material copy is unwritable, and the read count held CONSTANT across a record whose placements were multiplied over the same candidates, observed at the command by a stub gateway counting the reads it served rather than read off the accounting the run printed about itself (kogaki#163: a self-reported count is the system's own explanation of what it did, which is not evidence of it). The artifact-counting and seam-reading blocks report CANNOT-DETERMINE where the served seam is absent rather than passing or failing. PLUS §13.4's THREE RENDERING PROPERTIES over the provenance-neighborhood screen (kogaki#303, story 1.45): every rendered suggestion NAMES the substrate that reached it, with a substrate-less row rendering an explicit undisclosed marker rather than an empty `reached by:`; denominators stated PER FAMILY and never pooled, read from the batch records' own family-keyed `members` rather than re-derived from the served element set, with a family carrying no `members` list rendering an explicit no-denominator note rather than `of 0`; and an unresolved reference NAMED WITH ITS VALUE while the 12 legacy `q_a/N/answer.md` batches must NOT be marked, which is what stops the property passing vacuously by marking everything. Asserted over the COMPOSED LINES via the exported `neighborhoodScreen`, not over the enumerator: an enumerator returning a disclosed structure that the screen prints bare satisfies story 1.44's block and ships the defect.

admission.contract: the boundary-receipt binding at the merge layer (specs/SPEC.md §4, kogaki#25): a consultation-map boundary whose trigger terms MATCH the branch, with ZERO receipts present, FAILS — which is what converts the map from advice an agent may remember into a carrier that binds on every PR. A PRESENCE CHECK OVER TWO DECLARED ENUMERATIONS (the map's entries, the branch's receipts), both named in the output because a coverage claim is a fraction OF an enumeration. It NEVER BRANCHES ON THE OUTCOME TOKEN and structurally cannot: it reads line one only, so `discriminating`, `covered-after-reframing` and `uncovered-after-N-framings` satisfy it alike — the obligation is TO ASK and never TO HAVE FOUND (as corrected for kogaki#32), and a check that passed on some outcomes and failed on others would be judging whether the consultation SUCCEEDED, which is the review lane's property. LINE ONE ONLY also keeps it independent of the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10), whose validation stays with check-consult-receipts.sh — that check's report-never-gate contract is not absorbed, redefined or deleted, because this one gates a DIFFERENT property. It BINDS PRESENCE, NOT ORDER: a receipt written after the code it should have preceded satisfies it exactly as one written before, nothing in this repository observes that ordering, and the gap is stated rather than assumed covered (observed live on the story-1.10 branch). THE ATTRIBUTION HALF IS CARRIER-LESS AND MARKED: line one names a pin, never a boundary, so one receipt satisfies every matched boundary and a PR touching two while consulting one passes — carrier-less by omission is the defect, carrier-less with a reopen trigger is admissible (topics/knowledge-architecture.md:52@ed47fbd). FALSE POSITIVES ARE ACCEPTED AND DISCHARGED rather than narrowed away: an incidental term match is answered by the same act a real one asks for, so a spurious match costs one consultation rather than a false verdict — the map's ratified accretion polarity preserved at gate severity (owner decision at implementation; narrowing to diff paths alone was considered and declined as a silent shrink of what the map binds). THE SOURCE SET IS DECLARED and so is what it could not read — diff paths, changed text (commit messages, PR body), and the linked issue body, with an unavailable source NAMED rather than passed over, since an instrument that reports absence without establishing it is the defect check-review-report.sh refuses one layer up; an unreadable or unparseable map is COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fails, in its own wording, because a fallback worded as a finding accuses. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, firing BOTH discriminating cases — matched+receipt passes, matched+none fails — plus source coverage, outcome-invariance, line-one-only, use-vs-mention, and the word-bound case that keeps short terms from matching inside longer words. AND THE PATH SET IS THE BRANCH'S OWN, COMPUTED AT THE FORK POINT (kogaki#264): CI supplies `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` — the base branch's TIP at event time — and `git diff A..B` is a tree diff rather than a range, so every file that landed on master after this branch forked entered the path set and matched a boundary, at DENY severity, naming a file the branch never touched; the neighbouring `git log` and `git rev-list` read the same string as a genuine range, so the report printed a truthful commit count beside a path set of a different span. Paths, commits and count now all read the FORK POINT's span, and the output NAMES the fork point and says when the supplied base has advanced past it. The repair is sited in the check and not in the workflow because `base.sha` is a truthful name for a truthful value whose other consumers read it only through range operators, and because no fixture in this repository can watch a YAML expression. It does NOT reopen the kogaki#126 decline of narrowing to diff paths alone — that decline rests on path matches being the reliable signal, which this defect poisoned — and adds no judgment clause: matcher, sources and output vocabulary are untouched
admission.runtime_ms_note: re-measured at this admission act (kogaki#264), on the convention the sibling entries state: a runtime is a measurement, and a stale number is not a wrong one. Median of five local runs at this member's own ci-tier position with BOUNDARY_SKIP_ISSUE_LOOKUP=1 so no network is in the figure: 452 ms (490/444/452/436/437) against 116 ms for the same file at origin/master b38bda1 (111/111/123/119/116). THE ~336 ms IS BOUGHT, NOT INCURRED, and what it buys is named: ~55 ms is the span fixture's scratch repository (one `git init`, four commits), and the rest is arm 5 re-running THIS FILE twice inside that repository. Arms 1-4 exercise `_branch_paths`; none of them notices if the LIVE site stops calling it, and that mutation reinstates kogaki#264 verbatim — measured, not assumed: with only arms 1-4 present the live-line mutant SURVIVED the whole suite, and with arm 5 it is CAUGHT. The unit of the property is a two-branch history, so the detector's is too (`match-the-detectors-unit-to-the-propertys-unit`). Inner runs skip the span fixture, which is what keeps the cost at two invocations rather than a recursion. 500 is declared with margin over the measured median rather than at it. Re-measure at the next admission act that touches this check.

admission.contract: the review lane's presence half (specs/SPEC.md §4 PR-gate clause, kogaki#34): asserts that a review-lane report EXISTS on the pull request for its CURRENT head AND that no finding in it is declared blocking and still open — the property is CONVERGED OR ESCALATED rather than reviewed-once (kogaki#34 amendment). The head sha is part of presence rather than decoration — a report written against an earlier push reviewed code the PR no longer proposes, so it is reported STALE rather than counted (proposals-carry-the-state-they-were-computed-against applied to the reviewing act). It reads the DECLARED SEVERITY FIELD and never the findings' prose: whether a finding IS blocking is the reviewer's judgment recorded in a typed record, whether the PR CONTAINS an open blocking one is a fact over that record — the two-layer split's own test rather than an exception to it. The no-open-blocking half is CARRIER-LESS and MARKED: an empty findings record satisfies it and nothing distinguishes a thorough review from one that looked at nothing, so it carries a reopen trigger (one PR that passed with an empty record and later needed correction) rather than being carrier-less by omission, which is the defect. THREE-VALUED, with the third value EARNED BY EVIDENCE: exactly one state is CANNOT-DETERMINE — a lookup that succeeded and established there is no pull request. gh missing, a failed call, or a PR whose head will not resolve are COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fail, because a gate that exits 0 whenever its own instrument is unavailable disappears silently in the condition where it matters. The head is resolved independently of the comments fetch and an unknown head is never 'present' — both were fail-open paths reachable through the documented injection route (PR #44 review). FINDINGS BIND TO THEIR REPORT SEGMENT: only findings under a report naming the CURRENT head gate, a stale segment's findings being that round's record rather than this head's state — an unsegmented union deadlocked the rally at its first real use, since clearing a round-1 finding would have required editing the round-1 comment against clause 4's every-round-leaves-its-record (PR #44 review, round 1). States in its own output what it does NOT carry: whether the report's author differs from the work's author is unobservable, because session identity is in neither git nor GitHub metadata (measured on PR #43 — PR author, every commit author and the comment author are one login), so the isolation half is an obligation in .claude/skills/review-lane/SKILL.md and is ADVICE rather than enforcement. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, because a check whose only exercise is the live path is untested wherever that path is unavailable. BLOCKING GATES ONLY WITH ITS JUSTIFICATION PRESENT (kogaki#72): a blocking finding carries [policy: <pin>] or [harm: <one line>] to gate; an unjustified blocking is downgraded to should by name, failing toward merge — presence is the fact read here, adequacy stays the lane's judgment. REPORTS AND FINDINGS COUNT ONLY FROM TRUSTED AUTHORS (kogaki#56): comments are fetched with their authors and filtered to the repository owner plus pipeline.json's merge_author_allowlist before parsing — an author-blind parse let any commenter on a public repo spoof presence with a hand-written token, or hold a PR hostage with a foreign blocking line; a dropped spoof-shaped comment is reported, never silently discarded, and the trust-assembly fixture pass discriminates both directions THE BOUNDARY-VS-RECEIPT RECORD IS PARSED AND PRINTED, NEVER GATED (kogaki#258): a fifth adjacent declaration, `boundary: <entry N> <covered|uncovered|cannot-determine> [receipt: <pin>]` plus the declared zero `boundary: none`, giving the review lane's dimension-2 record a shape a reader other than a human can enumerate — an obligation cannot be gated and needs its absence made visible, so an ABSENT record is printed as UNDECLARED and is never read as `no boundary touched`. It adds NO denial and claims none: the record is not a finding, does not count toward report-complete equality, and the embedded fixture pass asserts gate-neutrality by re-running every boundary case with the lines stripped and requiring an identical verdict AND THE SUCCESSOR'S DECLARED OBLIGATIONS ARE READ AND PRINTED, NEVER GATED (specs/SPEC.md §4 clause 11, kogaki#306, story 1.59): a PR whose DECLARATION TEXT — its PR body and its branch's commit messages, the author's artifacts rather than the reviewer's — carries `supersedes: #<N>` owes a disposition for every finding #<N> left open, a base that descends #<N>'s, and a diff that is not byte-identical to #<N>'s under a block that made a structural claim. SIX properties ride this member's EXISTING trigger rather than entering as new members: the trigger is one PR's review record at merge, which this check already computes, so a split would pay six loop costs for one occasion and buy no independent removal signal. TWO of the six are the ones a natural implementation misses and both are asserted in BOTH directions — a `carried: #N` naming an issue THIS merge closes is UNDISPOSED because the carrier does not outlive the merge (kogaki#335: `carried: #325` while #325 closed on the successor's merge), and the falsification stays SILENT on a PROCEDURAL block, which diagnosed nothing and therefore has no claim an unchanged diff could falsify (kogaki#335 again, whose rebased diff came out identical under a block that was procedural). Clause 8's `carried:`/`declined:` grammar is LENT rather than restated: it moved to lib/disposition.py and BOTH consumers load it, asserted mechanically by reading both files, because a second vocabulary for what happened to a finding is a synonym in a join key. THE BASE-POSTDATES PROPERTY IS A CHECK STANDING IN FOR A GATE AND SAYS SO ON EVERY RUN: clause 11 rules it a PROHIBITION whose layer is actor-level and outside this repository, so a green run here is NOT the prohibition being in force — `deferred-slot: cross-repo-merge-gate`. And 'contains the corrective merge' is NOT established: nothing in this repository names that commit, so the containment half is cannot-determine by construction and is never asserted

admission.efficacy_note: the clause-11 fixture pass constructs a successor whose disposition is PRESENT, WELL-FORMED and COUNTS, and whose merge closes the very issue it names, and asserts the reader reports it UNDISPOSED. Named as this member's case because it is the one a check written from clause 11's positive criterion passes without implementing — the natural check reads the line's presence and stops. Its outliving twin is asserted not to fire, so the case discriminates rather than merely firing. Seven mutations were run against the six properties and all seven were killed; the seventh was added BECAUSE a mutation survived — collapsing the unmoved-base row into the does-not-descend row was invisible to a fixture reading only the verdict, so the unmoved case earned its own key. The ROUNDS-OBSERVATION block (kogaki#290) shipped its four cases with their discrimination read by a reviewer and never demonstrated; that gap is closed at kogaki#292 - four mutations run against `_rounds_observation`, all four killed, each by a DIFFERENT case (prefix-match to equality kills the respelling case; dropping the completeness filter kills the fragment case; an off-by-one on the bound kills the three silent cases; removing the count from the printed line kills the crossing-named case). One near-miss is recorded with the table rather than dropped: the completeness mutation was first applied by string replacement and landed on the FIRST `if not counted(seg):` in the file, in another function, so the check passed and read exactly like a surviving mutant
admission.runtime_ms_note: re-measured at this admission act (kogaki#357), and the honest finding is that THIS MEMBER'S RUNTIME IS NETWORK-DOMINATED AND NOT STABLE. Two five-run samples taken hours apart on the same machine: median 1050 ms early, median 5090 ms later, with a 6470 ms outlier. The same file at origin/master measured 1020 ms and 5080 ms in the same two moments, so THE CLAUSE-11 ADDITION IS ~10-30 ms and the spread is entirely the `gh pr view` round trips this check has always made. Declared at 7000 to cover the observed worst case rather than at a median that a fast moment would flatter. THE PREVIOUS DECLARATION OF 90 WAS STALE BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE before this change and is corrected here rather than left; naming it keeps a pre-existing error from being misattributed to this story's diff. A first correction in this same act declared 1200, computed from the fast sample alone — recorded because a number measured once at a lucky moment is the defect this note is about, and it was made and caught inside one sitting. The stable half is worth stating separately: the in-process fixture suite is ~30 ms of the total and is what a reader wanting a loop-position figure should use. Re-measure at the next admission act that touches this check, and take more than one sample.

admission.contract: the event adapter's two contracts, both found broken in one held run (kogaki#65): the trigger fires ONCE PER CREATED PULL REQUEST rather than once per tool call, and it closes stdin on the sessions it spawns. The first was a re.search over the tool response — first match only — so a Bash call that created PRs #63 and #64 fired the sweep for #63 alone and #64 reached the presence gate unreviewed, with ~/.kogaki/review-trigger.log carrying no --pr 64 line at any position; the second is why both held-run reviewers reported their prompts contaminated with this repository's own driver source, reaching them through an inherited descriptor. Exercises pr_numbers() over six cases (multi-PR, single, duplicate, ordered, absent, empty) and asserts BOTH that main() routes through that function — an inlined regression would leave the fixture passing over dead code — and that the Popen closes stdin. States what it does NOT verify: that the hook is registered in .claude/settings.json, that the harness fires it, and that the spawned sweep accomplishes anything, all of which are occasions rather than logic and stay with the presence gate
admission.removal_signal: the trigger's replacement by a lane-layer invocation that fires the sweep for the PR it just created (kogaki#65 remedy 4's second half) — at that point the hook is the manual-creation fallback rather than the primary carrier, and a fixture over its extraction stops being the thing standing between a batched creation and an unreviewed PR

admission.contract: the external-dependency registry (specs/SPEC.md:69-80, specs/spec-external-deps/SPEC.md; kogaki#55): the capabilities this repository NEEDS but cannot install, declared in deps/registry.json and read at run time rather than assumed. The specimen is the held run on PR #51, where three obstacles — the spawned reviewer's tool grants, the repository's allow_auto_merge, the merge deny's install state — were ONE defect, all assumed and none declared, so an unmet dependency presented as a stall or as a grant that was silently impossible to exercise. Reads specs/spec-external-deps/deps-schema.json's field lists rather than restating them, the same single-carrier arrangement check-gate-carrier.sh has against gate-schema.json. CONFORMANCE IS ITS SUBJECT AND THE WORLD IS A REPORT: it fails on a malformed or incomplete entry and never on an unmet dependency — the schema's own never_fails_on list, the same split this registry's consult-receipts entry already records ('Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count'), because whether a setting elsewhere is flipped changes without anyone touching the diff under review. EVERY ROW IS RENDERED, INCLUDING THE ZEROES: each decidable verification is EXECUTED and its result printed present or absent, each non-decidable entry's typed `none: <why>` is printed as its own row rather than omitted (a reason is evidence, an omission is not), and an empty registry's zero is printed through the same code path a fixture asserts, because a silent pass is indistinguishable from a check that did not run. A READ THAT DID NOT COMPLETE IS NOT AN ABSENCE: a command exiting non-zero is COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH on its own row and never 'absent', and every read runs under a hard timeout so a hanging network call cannot cost the pre-push loop unboundedly. The non-member fallback is carried rather than promised: deps/registry.json's observed_non_members list is rendered whether empty or not, and a recorded non-member stating no reason FAILS — admit-with-disclosure made checkable, which is the load-bearing half of an enumeration that can never be complete. States what it does NOT carry: nothing in this repository DETECTS that an act depended on an undeclared capability, so that list is hand-written and the observation half is carrier-less with a reopen trigger rather than carrier-less by omission; and whether a declared read answers the question its `answers` line claims, and whether an absence_signature is the signature the absence really leaves, are judgment and route to kogaki#13. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network: 12 entry-shape cases (conformant and malformed both fired), the four verification-read states including the two never-fails-on cases asserted by state rather than only by not-failing, duplicate ids, both directions of the non-member fallback, and the empty-registry rendering
admission.removal_signal: a host-side read of a spawned session's grant set, or any harness surface that reports the capabilities a run will actually have BEFORE it runs — at that point the needed-capability question is answered by the host rather than by a declared enumeration this repository maintains by hand, and a registry whose entries are hand-written is the wrong carrier for it. Fires the day the third entry's typed `none:` becomes decidable
admission.removal_instrument:
probe: python3 - <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.load(open('deps/registry.json'))
    e = [x for x in d['dependencies'] if x['id'] == 'spawned-session-tool-grants']
except Exception as ex:
    print(f'probe precondition failed: {ex}', file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
if not e:
    print('probe precondition failed: entry spawned-session-tool-grants not found', file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
v = e[0].get('verification')
if not isinstance(v, dict) or 'decidable' not in v:
    print('probe precondition failed: entry spawned-session-tool-grants carries no verification.decidable field — an absent block is not a not-yet answer (kogaki#116)', file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
sys.exit(0 if v['decidable'] else 1)
PY

admission.contract: specs/spec-client-kit/SPEC.md §8.1 and §8.3: a consultation reaches the owner as Question, Answer and Conclusion, and the pin stays machine-facing — so the owner render composer emits no `consulted:`, no `request_id:` and no `@<sha>`. Both directions are carried, because a deny alone passes trivially on a composer that renders nothing: the pass also requires a Question line, a readable flattened Answer, the Conclusion slot LEFT TO THE AGENT, a truncation that states its own denominator, and an unreadable response rendering DIFFERENTLY from a genuine miss. A thin invoker holding no assertions of its own — the cases are pure functions of a served response and live with the composer at `policy/kit/bin/gateway-query.mjs --self-test`, the same arrangement `client-kit-install` states for the kit's own test. THE MEMBER'S SCOPE IS DECLARED IN ITS OWN OUTPUT ON EVERY RUN, pass included: it is a LEXICON GREP over coined identifiers and covers that sub-class only, over ONE enumerated surface. Text machine-facing in REGISTER while made of ordinary words passes here and still violates §8; the positive admission test that would reach it is §7 q4, a named slot and not built. Story 1.50 AC5 makes presenting this as complete coverage a criterion FAILURE, which is why the disclosure is unconditional rather than printed on a hit — a check that announced its limit only when it fired would be silent in exactly the state that misleads.

admission.removal_signal: specs/spec-client-kit/SPEC.md §7 q4 being FILLED — a positive admission test at one typed owner-surface seam. The served line this member is admitted under demotes a lexicon grep to a fast path BENEATH such a test, so the test's arrival is what makes this member's continued existence a judgment rather than the only thing standing there; whether it is then deleted or kept as the fast path is that sitting's call, and this signal proposes the row rather than the deletion.
admission.removal_instrument: act: the decision act that fills §7 q4 — filling a named slot is itself a decision act owing its choice, alternatives and receipt on its licensing issue, and that sitting owes this member's removal row in the same act. Event-shaped and mechanically decidable: q4 is either struck-as-filled in the spec or it is not.
admission.efficacy_note: The counterfactual is sited with the composer because this member is a thin invoker holding no assertions of its own. The case drives the composer toward emitting the served `consulted:` line and `request_id` it holds in hand — which is what the pre-§8 kit did — and asserts refusal; and it drives the opposite collapse, a block that renders nothing and so satisfies every deny, asserting that fails too.
